notes: IEF 1.0 always + 1.0 extra IEF in TSYCAL's windows (last 3 trading days of the month OR +-1 day around scheduled FOMC decisions); financing T-bills + 50bp on gross > 1 (script wrapper); bench IEF; 2002-08+; TSYCAL as an overlay so active return = calendar excess return

red_team.summary: The result is real as far as the 2002-2024 data can show: holding extra 7-10y Treasuries only on month-end and FOMC days beat simply holding IEF by about 2.6-3%/yr, even after charging for the extra exposure, and no look-ahead, data error or 'just more duration' explanation survived testing (the government's own 10-year yield data show the same pattern, and fake shifted windows never come close). The caveats are practical: about half the gain came from 2008-2011, the edge is thin enough that paying Schwab's normal margin rate or sloppy fills (6bp a trade) would wipe out its statistical significance, and the strategy still loses money whenever bonds fall, as in 2021-2024 - it does not reduce the worst drop. It should be traded with Treasury futures or very cheap financing, not retail margin.
